# ayt — All You need is Text

ayt is a small, token-cheap planning loop for coding agents. You describe an idea, ayt turns it into a plain-text ticket with testable acceptance criteria, your agent implements it test-first, ayt reviews it against the ticket, and you open a PR that maps every ticket to its evidence. It's a set of Agent Skills (one `SKILL.md` each), so it runs in Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity (`agy`), Cursor and pi.

## Install

```sh
./install.sh --list          # show supported harnesses and where each installs
./install.sh                 # Claude Code (default)
./install.sh codex agy pi    # others; `all` for every one
./install.sh --project ...   # into the current repo instead of your home dir
```

## Use

```
/ayt-init → /ayt-new-idea → /ayt-implement → /ayt-review → (you commit) → /ayt-pr → /ayt-pr-review
              /ayt-bug ──────────┘                 /ayt-docs any time
```

Invocation differs by harness (`$ayt-new-idea` in Codex, `/skill:ayt-new-idea` in pi); see the main [README](../README.md#install).

## Test

There's no test runner: lint with `bash -n install.sh` (and `shellcheck install.sh`), and check a changed skill by running it on a scratch repo.
